purpose: Measure whether one additional warm Coder-7B replica can absorb the same offered workload when single-replica SLO goodput stalls. Reference is both off arms of the registered pressure experiment: same exact 8-slot binaries, arguments, host, C4/C8/C16/C16 30ms grid, fixture seeds and no previews. New run on two independent A100 replicas. Simple workflow round robin by arrival index; all three calls stay on the chosen replica. Do not compensate for the correlated role ordering. Report replica-specific cache and batches; different replica histories are part of this deployment policy.
protocol: Start both same-revision diagnostic servers through their original dedicated leases. Warm each once with seed 5091. Use a single origin and drain clock across both endpoints. Compare matched per-seed answers and timing from each scheduled arrival; charge two GPU-seconds per wall second. Include separately each server's lifetime inside its lease including startup and idle wait for its peer. Retain every failed job. This is one paired deployment on a single host, not independent nodes, autoscaling speed or steady-state capacity.
gate: At C16 require more SLO jobs and more warm SLO completions per allocated GPU-hour than both independent single-replica runs. Report raw completions per allocated GPU-hour, prefill rows, cached tokens, per-stream gaps and overall worst completion, low-load cost crossover and per-device active members. Require all baseline-valid jobs remain valid. No auto-release default.
